claims.text: Homogenization produces a uniform distribution of Cr and Al in the proposed high-entropy alloy.
A uniform elemental distribution and high configurational entropy establish a sluggish diffusion regime.
The sluggish diffusion regime maintains consistent availability of Cr and Al for selective, simultaneous oxidation.
Selective oxidation of Cr and Al forms a CrTaO4-based oxide containing minor Al2O3.
The resulting CrTaO4-based oxide is continuous, dense, and protective.
The protective oxide layer is self-healing.
A CrTaO4 layer can hinder outward elemental diffusion and reduce inward oxygen diffusion.
Species transport through the alloy, oxide/metal interface, and oxide layer governs high-temperature oxidation behavior.
Intentional microsegregation causes non-uniform oxide nucleation because of local compositional fluctuations.
Uneven elemental availability produces thicker, porous oxide scales and accelerates oxidation.
The homogenized alloy will have lower oxidation-induced net weight gain than the microsegregated alloy.
The homogenized alloy will form a more continuous and adherent CrTaO4-based scale with minor Al2O3 than the microsegregated alloy.
The homogenized alloy will resist oxygen diffusion more effectively than the microsegregated baseline.
Discontinuous Al2O3 and Cr2O3 dispersions do not provide an effective oxidation barrier.
The proposed mechanism applies to Cr- and Al-bearing high-entropy alloys oxidized at 1000–1100 °C for approximately 200 hours.
Grain size, secondary phases, and minor processing differences may influence oxidation behavior and confound the effect of compositional homogeneity.

contradictions.description: The specified example alloy AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 and the stated Co–Cr–Fe–Ni–X family with X = Al/Ti contain no Ta, yet the central predicted oxide is CrTaO4. No Ta source or Ta-bearing alternative composition is specified.

The predicted-outcome text suggests refutation when both scale characteristics and weight gain are similar, whereas the formal falsification rule uses disjunctive criteria under which failure of any single expected observation is sufficient. The decisive falsification condition is therefore inconsistent.
